one_sentence_story: John O'Keefe's 1971 discovery of hippocampal 'Place Cells' ('you are here') and May-Britt and Edvard Moser's 2005 discovery of entorhinal 'Grid Cells' (a 60-degree hexagonal coordinate ruler) revealed the brain's internal GPS — winning the 2014 Nobel Prize and showing how spatial maps also organize human memories and ideas.
so_what_for_you: Wake up your hippocampal-entorhinal GPS in daily life: orient yourself to real landmarks before turning on turn-by-turn navigation, and place tough facts inside vivid 'Memory Palace' rooms so Place Cells lock them in.
